items.title: Presentations and Announcements
Stephanie Toohill from the Save Middlebrook Bridge group provided an
notes: overview of the history of the bridge, noting its construction in 1910 and its relocation to its current position in 1946. She indicated the bridge has significant heritage value as a rare structural example of a pin-connected steel truss camelback truss bridge.

Mark Walker from the Save Middlebrook Bridge group noted the significance of the bridge, indicating it is a safe connector route for Active Transportation to trails and to many low traffic rural roads. He also noted it is an access to a nature point of the Grand River, pedestrian access to the Grand Valley Trailway, a visiting place of natural beauty for wildlife observation and a popular brown trout fishing area.
Mark Walker indicated the group is advocating for the rehabilitation of the bridge as:

1. A safe connector route for Active Transportation to the G2G, Cottontail Road Trail, Elora-Guelph trail, Grand Valley hiking trail, Trans-Canada Trail and to many low traffic rural roads away from dangerous vehicular roads;
2. An “Access to Nature Point” to the Grand River heritage watershed;
3. Pedestrian access to the Grand Valley Trailway;
4. A rare structural example of a pin-connected steel truss bridge. One of only four surviving truss bridges in Waterloo Region as noted in the Cultural Heritage Impact Statement;
5. An important and well known historic landmark via river or land that offers connection to our heritage, rural landscape and sense of place as part of the Grand Watershed Trails Network;

items.title: A visiting place of natural beauty for wildlife observation and popular
notes: brown trout fishing point.
He also noted the group has investigated potential sources for funding.
The Municipal Clerk provided procedural advice on how to bring forward a motion for reconsideration.

Stephanie Toohill and Mark Walker responded to questions regarding fundraising, consultation with the Mennonite community, discussions with the Township of Woolwich and they provided clarification on their desire to maintain the historic bridge for pedestrian traffic only. They indicated they are requesting Council reconsider the previous decision to remove the bridge and hold an additional public meeting.

5.2 Janet Harrop, President Wellington Federation of Agriculture provided background and current statistics on agricultural land and activity. She outlined the impact of Bill 97 and provincial policy statement changes affecting Wellington County. She noted the Federation is not supportive of the proposed lot creation policies which will lead to the loss of farmland, and also impact farms in many ways ranging from impacts on land values, to trespass, to road safety, to concerns over odour, dust, noise, etc. J.
Harrop noted the new lot creation policy will ultimately reduce opportunities to create and expand livestock in Ontario.

items.title: Consideration of Reports
2023 to 2026 Strategic Plan
notes: Report from D. Wilson, Chief Administrative Officer
Presentation by Dave Augustyn & Jordan Mammoliti from Augustyn Enterprises

D. Wilson, Chief Administrative Officer provided an overview of the report presenting the 2023 to 2026 comprehensive strategic plan. He indicated following the presentation from Dave Augustyn & Jordan Mammoliti from Augustyn Enterprises, additional information will be provided regarding business planning and advisory committees.
Dave Augustyn & Jordan Mammoliti from Augustyn Enterprises introduced the 2023 to 2026 strategic plan as a living document to help guide Council and staff.

Jordan Mammoliti outlined the project launch which included a full document review and environmental scan of local Municipalities, a SWOT (strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and threats) analysis and feedback from the senior management team. She noted the extensive public consultation process and the numerous Council and staff workshops to develop the Strategic Plan Framework, including the Vision, Mission, and Values.
Dave Augustyn provided an overview of the process followed to establish the vision, mission and values in the strategic plan. Jordan Mammoliti outlined the goals and priorities established.

D. Wilson reiterated the importance of the strategic plan in assisting Council and staff to set the priorities each year. He noted the corporate business plan is a key component linking the annual budget to the strategic plan. D. Wilson outlined the process to develop the corporate business plan and associated report card.

D. Wilson outlined the proposed advisory committee structure directly connected to the strategic plan. This structure includes existing committees such as Heritage Centre Wellington and the Diversity, Equity & Inclusion Advisory Committee and proposes two additional advisory committees, Economic Prosperity and Growth Advisory Committee and the Healthy Communities Advisory Committee, including two working groups the Activity, Health and Wellness working group and the Active Transportation and Environment working group.
D. Wilson outlined he next steps, including the development of the terms of reference for each committee, resident nominations and Council appointments.
Staff responded to questions regarding ensuring a youth representative or voice, benchmarking success or the report card, and highlighting and recognizing volunteers.

Councillor Wilton noted the plan was a result of collaboration between Council and staff, and expressed concerns that there is no mention of business attraction and retention, the significant or importance of water and attainable or affordable housing.
Dave Augustyn noted because the strategic plan is a living document, new goals and initiatives can be added through the corporate business plan process.

items.title: Ministry of Municipal Affairs and Housing Approval of Wellington County
notes: OPA 11
Report from B. Salmon, Managing Director of Planning and Development Presentation from Sarah Wilhelm, Manager of Policy Planning, County of Wellington

Sarah Wilhelm, Manager of Policy Planning, County of Wellington, indicated OPA 119 implements the County’s growth structure and is part of the municipal comprehensive review. The amendment was approved by the Province with modifications.

S. Wilhelm provided an overview of the modifications, including approval of the employment area conversion in Elora (supported by Watson & Associates technical analysis), the submission by the applicant for the Fergus Golf Course Recreational/ Residential Area, and the boundary expansion not originally part of OPA 119 but amended by the Province.
She outlined the approved urban expansions of 416 ha (1,030 ac) exceeds the results of Watson’s technical work.

S. Wilhelm indicated the next steps include a status update report in June to the County of Wellington Planning Committee, continuing to review other boundary expansion requests received to date and indicated the County will continue to work closely with the Township on our approach.

S. Wilhelm and B. Salmon, Managing Director of Planning and Development responded to questions regarding the further review of the other boundary expansion requests, status of Watson & Associates study, and provided clarification regarding servicing, phasing and staging of services to assist Centre Wellington with the additions to the urban boundary.
